c073.title: Aunt Iryna's Doctorate
c073.story: Anna's aunt Iryna finally finished her [[doctorate]] in sociology this fall. In October, Anna went with her to her [[alma mater]] in Lviv. The university held a big [[symposium]] there, and Iryna gave the opening talk. Her main [[argument]] was simple: public [[discourse]] online is getting too angry. "People stop listening; [[ergo]], they stop learning," she said. After the talk, the dean asked her to help write a new [[curriculum]] on media. Iryna enjoyed the [[prestige]] of the invitation, but she was happiest about the work. On the train home, Anna called her a real [[intellectual]]. "You have a great [[intellect]], Aunt Iryna!" she said. Iryna laughed. "No, I just read a lot of books."

c074.title: Anna Has a Virus
c074.story: Anna feels bad today, so she visits the [[doctor]]. The doctor checks her [[pulse]]. Then she uses a [[thermometer]]. It says 38 degrees! She asks Anna about her [[symptoms|symptom]]. Anna has a headache and a sore throat. "It is a [[virus]]," the doctor says. "You do not need an [[antibiotic]]. Take an [[aspirin]], 500 [[milligrams|milligram]], twice a day." The next morning, Anna feels much better. The medicine has a good [[effect]].

c075.title: Max at the Clinic
c075.story: Max has a busy morning at the city clinic. First, he checks in at the [[front office]]. His tooth hurts, so the dentist gives him an [[anesthetic]]. "You may need an [[implant]] one day," she says. She also tells him to use [[floss]] every night. "And wear your [[retainer]], please!" Next, a skin doctor checks his [[acne]] and gives him a cream. Finally, an eye doctor looks at his [[retina]]. "Your eyes are fine. You don't need [[laser]] surgery," she says. Max leaves the clinic tired but happy.

c076.title: Dad's Yearly Checkup
c076.story: Anna's dad has his yearly [[checkup]] on Monday. The doctor says his [[cholesterol]] is a little high. She asks about his [[risk factors|risk factor]], like smoking and stress. She sends him for a [[stress test]] and a cancer [[screening]]. She also wants him to see a heart [[specialist]]. "Do you still get [[migraines|migraine]]?" she asks. "Only on Mondays," Dad jokes. The clinic's [[case management]] team also helps Grandpa. They check his [[pacemaker]] and his [[insulin]]. They also look at the [[tremor]] in his hands. In the evening, Dad and Grandpa eat a healthy salad together.

c077.title: Anna's Healthy Lifestyle
c077.story: This year, Anna wants a healthier [[lifestyle]]. First, she stops eating [[junk food]] after classes. She buys [[vitamins|vitamin]] and fish oil with [[omega-3]]. Every morning, she puts bananas and milk in the [[blender]]. She drinks a big [[smoothie]] before class. After [[yoga]], she has a drink with [[electrolytes|electrolyte]]. On the weekend, she even tries a juice [[detox]]. In the evenings, she reads about [[metabolism]] and [[wellness]] online. At last, she shows Max a new [[anti-aging]] cream. "Anna, you are nineteen!" Max laughs. "Okay, maybe I don't need this one," Anna says with a smile.

c078.title: Talking About Stress
c078.story: Before her exams, Anna is under a lot of [[stress]]. Some nights she feels [[discomfort]] in her chest and cannot sleep. Max tells her to visit the college counselor, a kind woman named Olena. Olena asks Anna to write down every [[trigger]] that makes her anxious. They also talk about Anna's [[phobia]] of speaking in front of big groups. Olena teaches her simple [[coping]] skills, like slow breathing and short walks. "A calm, positive [[mindset]] really helps," she says, "and so does a little [[optimism]]." She gives Anna a [[self-help]] book and a weekly [[stress management]] plan. Asking for help is brave, she says, even with the [[stigma]] around mental health. Later that week, she gives every student a hotline number for thoughts of [[suicide]] or [[self-harm]]. Anna passes her exams, and she keeps the book on her desk.

c079.title: Grandma Remembers Lockdown
c079.story: On a rainy evening, Anna asks Grandma about the [[COVID]] years. "The whole city was in [[lockdown]] for weeks," Grandma says. "A virus is a kind of [[pathogen]], so we all stayed home. In winter, [[influenza]] was dangerous too. Your grandpa got [[pneumonia]] and went to the hospital. He needed [[oxygen]] and careful [[monitoring]] for five days. I stayed in [[quarantine]] at home and called him every day. Later, we both got a [[booster]] shot." Anna hugs her. "I'm glad those days are over, Grandma."

c080.title: An Accident in the Street
c080.story: On Monday, Anna sees a man fall off his bike. She feels a rush of [[adrenaline]] and calls for help. The [[dispatcher]] sends an ambulance right away. Two [[paramedics|paramedic]] arrive in five minutes. The man is in [[shock]] and has head [[trauma]]. They give him [[morphine]] for the pain. At the hospital, a doctor's [[pager]] beeps, and she runs to him. The man is in a [[coma]] for one day. He needs blood from a [[donor]]. His wife is in great [[distress]], so Anna stays with her. The next evening, the man wakes up and smiles at them.

c081.title: Health Week at College
c081.story: During health week, Dr. Kovalenko visits Anna's college to give a sex education class. She shows a clear diagram of the [[penis]] and the [[vagina]] and explains how they work. Then she explains how a [[hormone]] like testosterone can change your mood and body. Stress and poor sleep can lower your [[libido]], she says. She also explains what an [[orgasm]] is, in calm, scientific words. Next, she shows how to use a [[condom]] correctly to stay safe. She tells the students that a [[tampon]] is safe if you change it often. Infections like [[herpes]] and [[syphilis]] are common, but doctors can test for them and help. Finally, she says that [[porno]] is not real life and gives a wrong picture of love. Nobody laughs, and many students stay after class to ask questions. Max says it is the most useful class of the year.

c082.title: Uncle Petro's Way Back
c082.story: Anna's uncle Petro is an [[alcoholic]], and the family has worried about him for years. Last spring, after a long fight with [[alcoholism]], he finally went to [[rehab]]. He also stopped smoking, because he did not want [[nicotine]] to control him too. In his support group, people have very different stories. One woman used [[heroin]] and other [[opiates|opiate]] for ten years. A young man talks about [[cocaine]] and [[meth]] and the friends he lost. Another man started with [[marijuana]] at parties and later tried [[LSD]]. A woman explains how [[amphetamine]] pills ruined her sleep and her job. An older man takes [[methadone]] every day to stay away from street drugs. Petro listens to everyone and feels less alone. On Sunday, he comes to family dinner, drinks only tea, and Anna hugs him.

c083.title: The Big Derby on TV
c083.story: Max's dad is a big [[football]] [[fanatic]]. Tonight, they watch the city [[derby]] on TV together. The [[match]] is Kyiv Reds [[versus]] Kyiv Blues. In the first half, the [[referee]] calls a [[foul]] on the Reds. Later, he calls an [[offside]], and Dad shouts at the TV. In the second half, the Reds' [[goalkeeper]] saves a penalty. It is 1-1, so the game goes into [[extra time]]. In the last minute, a [[midfielder]] passes to the fast [[winger]]. He scores the winning [[goal]]! Max and his dad jump up and watch the [[replay]] five times.

c084.title: Max at the Gym
c084.story: Max wants to do more [[sport]] this year. He joins a [[club]] with a big [[fitness center]]. His [[trainer]], Oleh, is a [[guru]] with many online followers. Oleh makes a plan to improve Max's [[fitness]]. Max does twenty minutes of [[cardio]] and some [[stretching]]. On Fridays, he even goes to a [[pilates]] class. One day, an older man shows Max his huge [[biceps]] and [[six-pack]]. "I use [[steroids|steroid]]," he says. "Do you want some?" "No, thanks," Max says. "I want to stay healthy." After the workout, he books a long massage instead.
